import themepack
	bits = (value + '|||').split('|')
	theme = bits[0]
	# The filter rides in the key, so typing re-reads the list. 150
	# values is ten screens of scrolling to reach one token.
	needle = bits[3].strip().lower()
	if not theme:
		return []
	try:
		rows = themepack.all_tokens(theme)
	except Exception:
		return []
	if needle:
		rows = [r for r in rows
		if needle in r['name'].lower()
		or needle in (r.get('what') or '').lower()
		or needle in (r.get('group') or '').lower()
		or needle in (r['value'] or '').lower()]
	out = []
	last = None
	for r in rows:
		group = r['group']
		out.append({'group': group if group != last else '',
		'name': r['name'],
		'what': r.get('what', ''),
		'swatch': r['swatch'],
		'value': r['value']})
		last = group
	return out

import themepack
	# Always SWATCH_COUNT entries, never a short list: each chip binds to a
	# fixed index, so [] puts all sixteen bindings in error and draws the
	# palette as sixteen red boxes.
	empty = [''] * 16
	theme = (value + '|||').split('|')[0]
	if not theme:
		return empty
	try:
		return themepack.swatches(theme) or empty
	except Exception:
		return empty

import themepack
	# The colour to paint the chip, or nothing. Never the raw value:
	# CSS ignores what it cannot parse, so an invalid one left the
	# chip showing the PREVIOUS colour and reading as success.
	return value if themepack.looks_like_colour(value) else ''

props.text: Make a theme of your own: copy one of the ten, then change its colours here. The ten themselves are generated from the repo and Install overwrites them, so they are read-only on this page -- a copy is yours and nothing overwrites it.

transforms.code:
import themepack
	# Say what each one IS. The label was '(not ours)', which is true
	# of a theme you just made and reads as a disclaimer about it.
	suffix = {'user': '  (yours)', 'stock': "  (Ignition's)"}
	out = []
	for r in themepack.list_themes():
		kind = themepack.theme_kind(r['id'])
		out.append({'value': r['id'],
	'label': r['id'] + suffix.get(kind, '')})
	return out

import themepack
	theme = (value + '|').split('|')[0]
	if not theme:
		return ''
	kind = themepack.theme_kind(theme)
	# base_of() answers from the built-in tables, so for a theme made
	# here it falls through to 'light' -- and called every copy of a
	# dark theme light.
	base = (themepack.user_base_of(theme) if kind == 'user'
	else themepack.base_of(theme))
	# Plain ASCII, and a sentence rather than dash-separated fragments.
	# A non-ASCII character in a Jython 2 str literal is BYTES, not a code
	# point: the separator here arrived on the page as mojibake.
	words = {
		'packaged': '%s is one of the ten pre-packaged themes, built on %s. Install on the first page puts it back.',
		'stock': "%s is one of Ignition's own, built on %s. Editing it changes every project using it.",
		'user': '%s is yours, built on %s. Nothing on the Installer page overwrites it.',
	}
	# The NAME leads: the badge always says which theme it describes,
	# so after a create -- when the picker is the only other thing
	# naming it -- the page still names it somewhere.
	text = words.get(kind, kind)
	if '%s' in text:
		text = text % (theme, base or 'a stock theme')
	return text

	self.view.custom.new_base = self.view.custom.theme

	self.view.custom.status = ''

import themepack
	theme = self.view.custom.theme
	try:
		if themepack.delete_theme(theme):
			self.view.custom.status = 'Deleted %s' % theme
		else:
			self.view.custom.status = 'There was no %s to delete' % theme
		# Land on another theme rather than on an empty picker: the
		# dropdown's default only evaluates once, so clearing it leaves
		# 'Select...' and an editor with nothing in it.
		rows = themepack.list_themes()
		mine = [r['id'] for r in rows if r['ours']]
		self.view.custom.theme = (mine or [r['id'] for r in rows] or [''])[0]
		self.view.custom.file = 'variables.css'
		self.view.custom.nudge = self.view.custom.nudge + 1
	except Exception as e:
		self.view.custom.status = str(e)

	self.view.custom.new_name = ''
	self.view.custom.status = ''

import themepack
	name = (self.view.custom.new_name or '').strip()
	try:
		# make_theme copies one of ours, or builds on a bare Ignition
		# theme, depending on what was chosen -- one action, because
		# two buttons made them look like comparable alternatives.
		themepack.make_theme(name, self.view.custom.new_base)
		self.view.custom.new_name = ''
		self.view.custom.making = ''
		# nudge FIRST: it is what re-reads the theme list, and a
		# selection the options do not contain yet shows as blank.
		self.view.custom.nudge = self.view.custom.nudge + 1
		self.view.custom.theme = name
		self.view.custom.file = 'variables.css'
		self.view.custom.status = ('Created %s from %s -- it looks exactly like it until you change something'
		% (name, self.view.custom.new_base))
	except Exception as e:
		self.view.custom.status = str(e)

import themepack
	name = self.view.custom.undo_name
	was = self.view.custom.undo_value
	if not name:
		return
	try:
		themepack.set_any_token(self.view.custom.theme, name, was)
		self.view.custom.status = 'Put %s back to %s' % (name, was)
		self.view.custom.sel_name = name
		self.view.custom.sel_value = was
		# One level, and it is spent. Two Undos in a row putting the
		# same value back twice would be a button that lies.
		self.view.custom.undo_name = ''
		self.view.custom.undo_value = ''
		self.view.custom.nudge = self.view.custom.nudge + 1
	except Exception as e:
		self.view.custom.status = str(e)

import themepack
	name = self.view.custom.sel_name
	if not name:
		self.view.custom.status = 'Pick a value in the list first'
		return
	value = self.view.custom.sel_value
	try:
		# set_any_token finds the file: --st-* live in globals.css and
		# Ignition's own names in variables.css, and the page never showed
		# the user which is which. It also refuses a value that would
		# stop the token working, which is why this can fail loudly.
		result = themepack.set_any_token(self.view.custom.theme,
		name, value)
		# Remember what it replaced. Nobody remembers the hex they
		# overwrote, and there was no way back from a wrong save.
		self.view.custom.undo_name = name
		self.view.custom.undo_value = result.get('was', '')
		# Report the VALUE, not just the name: 'Saved --st-accent' is
		# equally true of a save that wrote back what was already there.
		self.view.custom.status = 'Saved %s = %s' % (name, value)
		self.view.custom.nudge = self.view.custom.nudge + 1
	except Exception as e:
		self.view.custom.status = str(e)

config.script:
import themepack
	theme = self.view.custom.theme
	filename = self.view.custom.file
	if not filename:
		self.view.custom.status = 'Pick a file first'
		return
	try:
		result = themepack.write_file(theme, filename,
		self.view.custom.text)
		self.view.custom.status = ('Saved %s (%d bytes) and scanned'
		% (filename, result['bytes']))
		self.view.custom.nudge = self.view.custom.nudge + 1
	except Exception as e:
		self.view.custom.status = str(e)

import themepack
	try:
		themepack.refresh()
		# Bump the key too, or the scan runs and every binding on this page
		# keeps showing what it read before it.
		self.view.custom.nudge = self.view.custom.nudge + 1
		self.view.custom.status = 'Scanned -- the gateway has re-read the themes'
	except Exception as e:
		self.view.custom.status = str(e)
